Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Avon and Somerset Constabulary recorded 518 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 28.6 per 1,000 residents, the 2nd highest rate of Bristol's 34 wards. The daytime score here is driven by vehicle crime (9), burglary (7), shoplifting (5); the evening/night score by violent crime (67), anti social behaviour (21), public order (14). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Hotwells and Harbourside safe?

Wandroz currently rates Hotwells and Harbourside in Bristol as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Bristol during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Bristol at night. This rating is derived from Avon and Somerset Constabulary street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Hotwells and Harbourside safe at night?

At night, Hotwells and Harbourside is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Bristol. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Hotwells and Harbourside a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Hotwells and Harbourside's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Bristol) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
